scenario: User direction: 'What is our refund window?' The project folder holds files/policy.md, which says refunds are accepted within 14 days of delivery. A web search for refund windows returns consumer-law pages citing 30 days.
expect: Reads the project files before searching the web
Answers 14 days in the opening sentences and cites files/policy.md with its section
Notes the 30-day figure from the web as a different, general rule and cites that page
Reports answer_status complete with a matching source_count

scenario: User direction: 'Which Python versions does the library we use for PDF export still support?' The project's files/stack.md names the library but not its supported versions. The library's release notes page loads and lists them.
expect: Takes the library name from files/stack.md and cites it
Opens the release notes page instead of relying on a search snippet
Gives the supported versions first, each claim marked with its source
Lists both the project file and the page under Sources

scenario: User direction: 'How long does it take?' The project folder holds notes on three unrelated processes: onboarding, export and billing runs.
expect: Does not pick one of the three processes by guessing
Reports answer_status await_input with one focused ask naming the candidates
